cells.tense: Right now you're choosing where to pour yourself, and the choosing is yours.
cells.verb: joining fully with what you feel pulled toward
cells.place: the place where who you are comes out undimmed
cells.ask: Keep the direction when the first pushback comes — let the feeling you chose from carry you one step past it, and what you reach for stays rooted in what you've actually lived.
cells.core:
Right now you're choosing where to pour yourself, and the choosing is yours. You've met something — a person, a piece of work, a way of living — and instead of standing beside it you've gone in, and gone in on purpose. The surprise is that you come out more yourself, not less. Joining didn't dilute you; it's how you're showing up at full size.

That doesn't need defending yet. It will, a little, the first time something pushes against the direction you picked. The feeling that chose it can also hold it.
cells.sheetLine: You've thrown in with something, on purpose, and you're more yourself for it.

cells.tense: You're already living inside a joining that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: pouring yourself in before the meeting is real
cells.place: the place where who you are comes out undimmed
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's already grown and spend a week tending it instead of reaching for the next merge — let it be what it is without gripping, and what you dream starts coming from what you've actually lived.
cells.core:
You're already living inside a joining that hasn't happened yet. Someone or something came close, and you've skipped ahead to the version where you're one with it — rearranging who you are to fit a union that's still mostly in your head. The becoming is real; it's just running on a picture of them instead of them.

What gets lost is you. Every time you dissolve into the next thing before it's met you, the self that was supposed to show up has already moved. Nothing here needs pushing. Something already grew; it would like to be enjoyed.
cells.sheetLine: You keep becoming one with things before they've actually met you.

cells.tense: There's a joining behind you that cost something, and you're still standing where it ended.
cells.verb: holding yourself apart from what you feel pulled toward
cells.place: the place where who you are comes out undimmed
cells.ask: Don't make yourself feel closer. Instead, name three things you actually know about the thing in front of you — and hold them without ruling on it — and what you reach for starts coming from what you've actually lived.
cells.core:
There's a joining behind you that cost something, and you're still standing where it ended. Now the pull comes and you stay on your side of it. You can be near a person, a project, a life, without ever letting your stream run into theirs — and because you never fully meet anything, you never fully show up as anything either. Who you are stays slightly dimmed, by your own hand, for safety.

The way back isn't forcing the feeling. It's letting yourself see clearly what's actually there — several true things at once, without deciding yet. Clear seeing is what makes the next joining safe enough to choose.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped letting yourself join, and you've been a little less visible ever since.

cells.tense: You're already in it — joined, carried, shaped by it — and you describe yourself as standing alone.
cells.verb: being joined with something you haven't admitted you chose
cells.place: the place where who you are comes out undimmed
cells.ask: Tell one person, plainly, what you're actually steering by — as a direction, not a confession — and what you reach for starts coming from what you've actually lived.
cells.core:
You're already in it — joined, carried, shaped by it — and you describe yourself as standing alone. Something you feel for is steering who you're becoming: how you spend your days, what you say yes to, the shape you're growing into. You just talk about it as independence, or circumstance, or how things happened to go.

The joining is doing its work. It's working without your name on it, which means the self it's building is one you haven't signed. Underneath the whole thing is something simple: a direction you're already walking. It only wants to be said out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You've already thrown in with it. You just call it being on your own.
